references.text: The regulation to use a male goat as a sin offering for a leader in Israel, showing the background for the sacrifice mentioned in Numbers 7:52.
Aaron offered a male goat as a sin offering, demonstrating the same sacrificial practice as at the dedication of the tabernacle.
The first time a male goat is mentioned as a sin offering in this series of dedications, with Nahshon's offering.
Parallel text where Netanel ben Zuar also offered a male goat as a sin offering.
Parallel text where Eliab ben Helon also offered a male goat as a sin offering.
Parallel text where Elizur ben Shedeur also offered a male goat as a sin offering.
Parallel text where Shelumiel ben Zurishaddai also offered a male goat as a sin offering.
A male goat is used as a sin offering for the entire congregation in cases of unintentional sin.
A male goat as a sin offering at the new moon sacrifice, showing the continuation of this sacrificial practice.
King Hezekiah ordered male goats to be offered as sin offerings for the kingdom, illustrating the use of this sacrifice in later times.
At the rededication of the temple after the exile, male goats were sacrificed as sin offerings.
The Old Testament sin offering with goat's blood points forward to Christ's perfect sacrifice that cleanses the conscience.
